### kinesis-data-streams-unhandled-processrecords-exception-skips-batch

**Claim.** An exception thrown from processRecords is absorbed by the KCL, and the KCL does not resend that batch of records. Consumers then see skipped records, so all exceptions must be handled inside processRecords.

**Write it as.** `does not resend the batch of records` · `absorbed by the KCL`

> "Any exception thrown from `processRecords` is absorbed by the KCL. To avoid infinite retries on a recurring failure, the KCL does not resend the batch of records processed at the time of the exception. The KCL then calls `processRecords` for the next batch of data records without restarting the record processor. This effectively results in consumer applications observing skipped records. To prevent skipped records, handle all exceptions within `processRecords` appropriately."
> — [Troubleshoot Kinesis Data Streams consumers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/troubleshooting-consumers.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-15.
